newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Russian troops kill two on Tajik-Afghan border.
newsitem.headline: Russian troops kill two on Tajik-Afghan border.

text.p: Russian border guards shot dead two people and detained a third trying to cross from Afghanistan into Tajikistan on Sunday, Russian military sources said.
"The three were drugs smugglers, probably Afghan nationals," a Russian military official told Reuters in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
He said the two were shot trying to cross near the Russians' Moskovsky border post on the Pyandzh River, about 250 km (150 miles) south of Dushanbe.
He said 20 kg (44 lbs) of raw opium were found on the bodies, bringing the total amount of raw opium seized in the last week by Russian border guards in Tajikistan to 100 kg (220 lbs).
Russia deploys about 20,000 troops in the remote, mountainous republic bordering Afghanistan and China, where they carry out peacekeeping duties and guard the country's border.
Sunday's deaths follow a spate of shootings along the Tajik-Afghan border in recent weeks.
Drugs traffickers have taken advantage of instability in Tajikistan, tentatively emerging from a four-year civil war, to smuggle narcotics produced in Pakistan and Afghanistan to Europe.
